text: Inventory discrepancy, Vatican Library 1503: Illuminated manuscript depicts Battle of Waterloo with historically accurate detail. Waterloo occurs in 1815. Manuscript vellum carbondated to 1388. Illuminator died of plague in 1502.

Architectural survey, Babylon 1750 BCE: Ziggurat contains elevator shaft with bronze call buttons. Cuneiform inscription reads Floor 7: Hanging Gardens. Gardens won't exist for 600 years. Shaft descends infinitely downward.
Autopsy report, County Coroner 1936: Subject died from exposure to element not discovered until 1940. Cause of death listed as acute berkelium poisoning. Element occurs naturally nowhere on Earth.

Seismic monitoring station, Chile 1960: Earthquake registered 9.5 magnitude but tremors occurred in alphabetical order by affected city name. Duration matched exactly with recitation of local phone directory from 1973.

Pleistocene mammoth remains, Siberia 14,000 BCE: Stomach contents include cultivated wheat varieties not developed until 1961. Grain shows evidence of industrial milling processes. Specimen otherwise anatomically consistent.

Papal bull issued 1347 lists official feast days for saints who won't be born until 1832. Vatican archives contain their authenticated relics dated 1298. Relics include fragments of synthetic materials.

Municipal water records, Phoenix 1952: Resident at 447 Oak Street consumed 847 gallons daily for six months. Property inspection revealed standard fixtures, single occupant. Occupant had been deceased since 1949.

Digital archive corruption, Library of Congress 1987: Database contains 40,000 card catalog entries for books that don't exist. When librarians attempt deletion, entries multiply. Books occasionally appear on shelves overnight.

Botanical survey, Amazon Basin 1889: Expedition catalogued tree species that photosynthesize moonlight. Specimens collected during new moon phases continued growing in complete darkness for eighteen months.

Archaeological anomaly 2019: Roman villa excavation, Pompeii, uncovered mosaic depicting WiFi symbol with Latin inscription SIGNAL WEAK HERE TOO. Tesserae composition authentic to 79 CE. Network name: VESUVIUSGUEST.

Personnel file, Sears Department Store 1963: Employee Harold Kemper worked register 7 for thirtyone years. Store only had six registers. Payroll continued until 1994. No record of Harold Kemper's hire date or existence.

Meteorological report, Damascus 1401: Clouds formed geometric patterns spelling out next week's grain prices in Arabic script. Predictions proved accurate to the dinar. Sky remained illiterate until 1823.

Census data, Prague 1572: Population recorded as 47,000 living residents plus 3,200 formerly living but administratively active. Tax records show the formerly living paid promptly. Death certificates for this group dated 1598.

Surgical report, Vienna General Hospital 1894: Patient's appendix contained fully formed pocket watch, ticking accurately. Timepiece showed correct hour despite patient never owning a watch. Inscription: Property of Future Self.
